market_holds: Sealed baseline (2026-11-10 18:10 UTC): spot 8.18, front-expiry straddle 15.3% and an event-implied move of 12.7% (the ATM spread is 48% of mid, so this is indicative only), 20d realised vol 115%. Seven prior prints have a median absolute move of 7.85% (3 up, 4 down): +7.85, -3.11, +8.36 for the three 2026 prints. The stock is -17% over 5d, -28% over 20d, -65% from its 52w high and 1.9% above its 52w low. It has given back about 50% since the Q2 print (finviz preview, 2026-11-03), and on my Yahoo bars it is down from 12.53 (2026-10-28, after SpaceX's 900 MHz filing) to 8.20 today, moving with the speculative space and spectrum basket (ASTS fell from 42.3 to 32.4 over the same days). Consensus is EPS -$0.12 on revenue of about $0.99m (finviz and Benzinga, early November). The company gives no guidance. FINRA short interest at the 2026-09-30 settlement was 21.2m shares with 8.9 days to cover, about 20% of float. The stock trades on the FCC Lower-900 MHz / PNT rulemaking, not on the quarter.
view: The quarter is about $1m of revenue, and GAAP results swing on non-cash derivative marks, so the reaction depends on what management says about the regulatory path and on any new commercial or partner news. I checked the regulatory path at its source. The FCC's PNT draft NPRM (WT 25-110, RIN 3060-AM01) still sits in the pending list at OIRA as of today, received 2026-03-02 and not concluded. The FCC's November 19 meeting carries drone, counter-drone and in-flight items in other bands, not this NPRM. The December tentative agenda comes out after the scored window. So the release almost certainly cannot announce a cleared NPRM or a vote date, and management will repeat 'subject to interagency review'. The market already holds that: the stock has fallen from about 12.5 to 8.2 since the November agenda came out without the item, and the 2026-11-03 preview headline already calls the rule stalled. Japan (the MIC 900 MHz allocation that gates the METCOM warrants) shows no new decision since the May 2026 partial report. The stock now sits at its lows with about 20% short interest and no new negative I can find, which makes a 'nothing new' print slightly more likely to bounce than to break. But the release could just as easily hold a softer timeline or a negative tone, and the stock trades with a risk-off speculative basket that fell again today. I see no edge I would bet on.

recommendation.reason: The line the stock trades on, the timing of the FCC PNT NPRM, is visibly stalled at OIRA, and the slide since late October already holds that. I found no dated, unpriced datapoint that this release would reveal. The washed-out positioning (52w low, about 20% short) tilts slightly up, but that is not a mechanism.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Management saying OIRA review has concluded or the NPRM is going to a vote, or a named commercial or government contract with dollar terms (up), against a statement that the FCC is reconsidering the band, a capital raise or a buyback-free cash burn rise (down).

self_critique: The 20% short interest and a 35% drop in two weeks into the print could make even a vague positive (a new partner, a Tier 1 911 rollout date, 'constructive engagement with OIRA') produce a squeeze bigger than the 12.7% implied move. Calling it neutral may understate a positive skew. Against that, the stock trades with a risk-off speculative basket that fell again today, and a pre-print slide without news can also mean informed selling I cannot see.
